description: The mission of Bread for the City is to help Washington, DC residents living with low income to develop their power to determine the future of their own communities. We provide food, clothing, medical care, and legal and social services to reduce the burden of poverty. We seek justice through community organizing and public advocacy. We work to uproot racism, a major cause of poverty. We are committed to treating our clients with the dignity and respect that all people deserve.

Our students participate in out-of-school-time art classes, workshops, open studios, field trips, and exhibition and performance opportunities.

description: The Career Path DC Clean and Safe Team serves as a resource within the District of Columbia by creating employment opportunities for the residents and creating a clean and safe environment within the communities we serve. We create employment opportunities for the City’s most needy residents, selecting participants from each of the eight Wards within the City. We provide these individuals with intensive life skills and job readiness training, focusing on obtaining and maintaining employment, acceptable workplace behaviors, and overcoming barriers. The participants also receive work experience training, learning the methods of beautification within living, working, and business environments.

org_name: Boys and Girls Clubs of Greater Washington
description: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Washington (BGCGW) traces its roots to 1886 as the Newsboys and Children's Aid Society, evolving through several name changes before becoming Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Washington in 1981 when it began serving both boys and girls equally. Its mission is to help young people, especially those who need it most, build confidence, develop character, and gain the skills to become productive, civic-minded adults.

Kid Power provides civics-based academic enrichment, hands-on science and gardening, and mentorship to DC youth in under-resourced neighborhoods. The organization empowers students to build academic skills, practice healthy living, and advocate for positive change in their communities.

Urban Ed provides technology-focused education, information technology certifications, and workforce development to children, youth, and adults in the DC region. Its programs address early educational gaps and equip residents with marketable technical skills for high-demand IT careers.

Bread for the World is a nonpartisan, Christian advocacy movement that works to urge national leaders to end hunger in the United States and across the globe. Through grassroots mobilization and legislative policy reform, it addresses the root causes of food insecurity

Christ Church Capitol Hill is a historic Episcopal parish in Washington, DC, offering inclusive worship and community fellowship. The church actively engages the local community through outreach initiatives, social justice efforts, and charitable partnerships.

New Image Community Baptist Church is a vibrant faith community located in Ward 7 focused on spiritual development and neighborhood fellowship. It actively serves local residents through community outreach, family support services, and local ministry initiatives.

Good Success Christian Church is a faith-based organization committed to spiritual growth, mentorship, and holistic empowerment. The ministry offers worship services alongside community outreach and educational workshops designed to support local families.

Ward Memorial AME Church is a long-standing African Methodist Episcopal congregation dedicated to social justice and community advocacy. Located in Ward 7, the church hosts worship services, food distribution initiatives, and youth development opportunities.

Run-Hope-Work supports DC youth and returning citizens by combining physical running training with hands-on construction trade education and job placement. The program uses fitness to build mental resilience while teaching market-ready job skills for long-term career success.

Founded in 2015, C. Jonez Nutrition Consulting Services, LLC (DBA Food Jonezi) is a Washington, D.C.-based health and wellness practice offering personalized nutrition counseling, education workshops, and healthy cooking classes. Serving a diverse audience—including Medicaid/Medicare participants, corporations, nonprofits, and government agencies—Food Jonezi has impacted over 9,000+ D.C. residents, facilitated 1,500+ workshops, and participated in 300+ community health fairs. Recognizing the greater need within underserved communities, Food Jonezi Friendz, its nonprofit arm, was launched in 2021 to focus on tackling food insecurity through culturally focused cooking classes, interactive workshops, and nutrition counseling. The nonprofit also introduced the Chef in Training program, equipping adolescents (ages 15-17) with essential food, nutrition, and culinary skills to foster healthier futures.

Southeast Welding Center provides hands-on vocational training in welding alongside trauma-informed support services for returning citizens and adults. The program offers technical skills, trade certifications, and job placement assistance to reduce barriers to long-term employment

ANC 7C is a local advisory body representing Ward 7 neighborhoods including Deanwood, Burrville, and Lincoln Heights. The commission serves as a bridge between residents and city officials on matters concerning local development, public safety, and infrastructure.

ANC 7F represents Ward 7 residents in neighborhoods such as Fort Dupont, Benning Heights, and parts of River Terrace. It gathers neighborhood input to advise DC government officials on public policy, local development, and municipal resources.

From early childhood education and youth services to housing counseling and job training, UPO is committed to creating pathways for individuals to thrive and build a better future.

Our mission is simple: Feed the Hungry, Give Drink to the Thirsty, and Clothe Those in Need. Our organization's mission intertwines Faith, Art, and Health to "Feed the Hungry, Give Drink to the Thirsty, and Clothe Those in Need" in the most creative ways possible. God has a soft spot in his heart for those suffering or at-risk of homelessness and we do too. Together we can Plant Love in the Hearts that Need it Most!

For over fifteen years, Project Empowerment has helped to reduce economic disparity in the District by serving thousands of individuals with multiple barriers to employment. The Program’s work readiness model is designed to provide nearly 700 unemployed District residents with opportunities to grow in education, training, and subsidized employment placements each year. Project Empowerment achieves its mission of moving participants into the workforce by partnering with government, non-profit, and private businesses across the DMV area to recruit, train, match, and coach candidates for successful employment.
